title: Great Barrier Reef Marine Park and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2008

divisions.question: Great Barrier Reef Marine Park and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2008 - Referral to Committee

speeches.speaker: Jan McLucas
speeches.brief: The minister moved to introduce the bills together, with a subsequent motion to list them separately on the Notice Paper, and the Senate agreed to proceed without formalities and read the bills a first time.

speeches.speaker: Jan McLucas
speeches.brief: The Great Barrier Reef Marine Park and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2008 updates the 1975 Act to improve protection, enforcement, and alignment with the EPBC Act, including restoring an Indigenous member to the Marine Park Authority. The Therapeutic Goods Legislation Amendment (Annual Charges) Bill 2008 sets uniform annual charge payment dates and strengthens transparency for low-turnover exemptions. The Financial Framework Legislation Amendment Bill 2008 simplifies financial management for Commonwealth agencies, allowing outsiders to make public money payments and clarifying that resource use must align with Commonwealth policies.

speeches.speaker: Steve Fielding
speeches.brief: A motion was moved to refer the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2008 to a Senate committee for inquiry by 10 November 2008, citing concerns that changes to definitions and the precautionary principle could ban recreational fishing. The Coalition supported the motion; the Greens and the Labor Government opposed it, arguing extensive consultation had already occurred.

speeches.speaker: Ian Macdonald
speeches.brief: The speaker argued for supporting the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park amendment bill while proposing amendments to expand the board to include a tourism/industry member and to expunge criminal convictions for minor fishing zone breaches. Senator Joyce raised concerns about overly broad definitions of "fishing" and the precautionary principle, advocating for a committee inquiry.

speeches.speaker: Ron Boswell
speeches.brief: Debate over the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2008 saw Senator Boswell propose an amendment to expunge the criminal convictions of 324 fishers caught in green zones before December 2006, citing the $255 million compensation package and the 33% of reef zoned as representative areas, while critics labelled the expanded definition of 'fishing' draconian. The Senate ultimately referred the bill to the Standing Committee on Environment, Communications and the Arts with a reporting date of 15 September 2008, while the government rejected pardons for the fishers and proposed an amendment to ban geological storage of greenhouse gases in the reef region.

speeches.speaker: Jacinta Collins
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the majority report on the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2008 was incorrect, stating that 324 people received criminal convictions for fishing offences without prior warnings, contrary to the report's claims. He highlighted the cases of Barry Garlick and Peter Aston, and moved an amendment to have those convictions treated as spent.

speeches.speaker: Stephen Parry
speeches.brief: Additional comments on the Environment, Communications and the Arts Committee’s report on the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2008 were tabled at the request of Senator Joyce.

speeches.speaker: Jan McLucas
speeches.brief: The opposition argued for an amendment to the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2008 requiring at least one board member to have tourism industry experience, and for a separate amendment to have criminal convictions spent for recreational fishers fined between 1 July 2004 and 14 December 2006 for entering green zones.

speeches.speaker: Judith Troeth
speeches.brief: The committee negatived Senator Joyce’s opposition amendments, then agreed to government amendments inserting a definition of “fishing” and prohibiting geological storage of greenhouse gases in the Great Barrier Reef. speeches.speaker: Jan McLucas
speeches.brief: The Coalition argued that Labor reneged on a pre-election commitment made by former Prime Minister John Howard to support the opposition's amendments, which would provide relief to ordinary Australians facing legal records. The bill was read a third time and passed with the Senate's support.
